record.paper_title: Structural results on circular-arc graphs and circle graphs: A survey and the main open problems
record.original_question: Characterize, by forbidden induced subgraphs, which chordal graphs are circle graphs. A circle graph is the intersection graph of chords on a circle, and a chordal graph is a graph with no induced cycle on four or more vertices. The desired characterization should identify exactly which induced subgraphs prevent a chordal graph from being representable as a circle graph.

evidence.quote: Problem 7. Characterize circle graphs by forbidden induced subgraphs within the class of chordal graphs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A graph G is called a circle graph if there exist a circle C and a family of chords of C in bijection with V(G) such that two vertices of G are adjacent if and only if the two corresponding chords intersect inside C. A graph is called chordal if it contains no induced cycle on four or more vertices.

Provide a characterization, by a complete list of minimal forbidden induced subgraphs, of those chordal graphs that are circle graphs. Equivalently, determine the (finite or infinite) family F of graphs such that a chordal graph G is a circle graph if and only if G contains no induced subgraph isomorphic to any member of F.
artifact.status_search_result: A complete forbidden induced subgraph characterization of circle graphs within the class of chordal graphs is not known. Progress has been made on subclasses: Bonomo-Braberman, Durán, Grippo, Safe, and others gave a characterization within split graphs (a subclass of chordal graphs) in a 2020 paper. The general chordal case remains open.

status_evidence.title: Forbidden induced subgraph characterization of circle graphs within split graphs
status_evidence.snippet: A structural characterization by minimal forbidden induced subgraphs for the entire class of circle graphs is not known, not even restricted to split graphs. In this work, we give a characterization by minimal forbidden induced subgraphs of circle graphs, restricted to split graphs.
status_evidence.claim: The characterization is known for split graphs (a strict subclass of chordal graphs) but the chordal case remains unresolved.
